method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), retrieved 2026-09-23. claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start resuscitation immediately if there are signs of hypoxia and/or shock**, to prevent progression to cardiorespiratory arrest.
claims.source_text: Commence immediate resuscitation if there are signs of hypoxia and/or shock to prevent progression to cardiorespiratory arrest
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Call early for help** within the hospital and to the local paediatric retrieval service.
claims.source_text: Call early for help within your hospital and to local paediatric retrieval service as necessary … Consider early referral to specialised paediatric/retrieval service
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **This page does not cover** trauma, neonates or children in cardiorespiratory arrest.
claims.source_text: This CPG is for seriously unwell children, it does not cover trauma and seriously injured children, neonates or children in cardiorespiratory arrest
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess and manage in parallel, and allocate roles early:** team leader · airway nurse and doctor · circulation nurse and doctor · primary survey doctor · scribe/timekeeper with a stopwatch · family support.
claims.source_text: Reactive resuscitation of seriously unwell children includes assessment and prompt management in parallel … Early allocation of roles can optimise resuscitation (if personnel available). Suggested roles: Team leader Airway nurse and doctor Circulation nurse and doctor Primary survey doctor Scribe and timekeeper with a stopwatch Staff member dedicated to family support
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep the child calm** (hands off, caregiver present, distraction), **let them keep their adopted posture**, and position the head: **under 1 year neutral, over 1 year sniffing.**
claims.source_text: Keep child calm (e.g. hands off approach, caregiver present, distraction techniques) Optimise head position to achieve patent airway Continue child’s adopted posture < 1y neutral position >1y sniffing position
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Airway adjuncts:** head tilt, chin lift, jaw thrust, oropharyngeal airway. ⚠️ **A nasopharyngeal airway is contraindicated with facial or base-of-skull fracture.** Consider PEEP in upper airway obstruction.
claims.source_text: Simple airway manoeuvre Head tilt Chin lift Jaw thrust Insert oropharyngeal airway Insert nasopharyngeal airway (contraindicated facial/base of skull fracture) … Consider PEEP in upper airway obstruction
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Not breathing: start artificial ventilation.** Otherwise give **oxygen 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask** and consider elevating the head of the bed.
claims.source_text: If the child is not breathing, commence artificial ventilation Consider elevating head of the bed Oxygen 15L/min non rebreather mask
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-invasive options:** high-flow nasal cannulae, CPAP, BiPAP.
claims.source_text: Non-invasive ventilation High flow nasal canulae CPAP BiPAP
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use a self-inflating bag on a spontaneously breathing child** — it delivers oxygen only when squeezed. A T-piece/Neopuff can give PEEP.
claims.source_text: Do not use self-inflating bags in spontaneously ventilating patients, they are designed to deliver O2 only if squeezed … T-piece/neopuff may be used to administer PEEP
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Secondary signs of inadequate oxygenation:** tachy- or bradycardia, pallor or cyanosis, cool peripheries, altered mental state.
claims.source_text: Secondary signs of inadequate oxygenation: tachy or bradycardia, colour change (pale or blue), cool peripheries, altered mental state
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypotension is a late, pre-terminal sign** — use the correct cuff size.
claims.source_text: Hypotension (hypotension is a late and preterminal sign) *ensure correct cuff size
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Secondary signs of poor circulation:** tachypnoea without increased work of breathing, or bradypnoea; altered conscious state; pallor or cyanosis.
claims.source_text: Secondary signs: tachypnoea (especially if no increased work of breathing) or bradypnoea; altered conscious state; colour change (pallor or cyanosis)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No signs of circulation — no pulse, pulse below 60, or unsure — start external cardiac compressions**, then determine the rhythm and treat it.
claims.source_text: If there are no signs of circulation (no pulse, slow pulse <60 or you are not sure) commence external cardiac compressions Determine cardiac rhythm and treat accordingly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Two large-bore IV cannulas; intraosseous if IV access is not prompt.**
claims.source_text: 2 large bore intravenous cannulas Insert intraosseous cannula if unable to gain IV promptly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fluid bolus 10–20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9%, up to 40 mL/kg.** Consider sepsis and inotropes/vasopressors; correct electrolytes.
claims.source_text: Fluid resuscitation Fluid Bolus 10-20ml/kg Sodium chloride (NaCl) 0.9% (up to 40ml/kg) Consider sepsis Consider inotropes/vasopressor Correct electrolytes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess AVPU/GCS, pupils, focal deficit, seizure activity and toxin exposure.**
claims.source_text: AVPU/modified GCS/GCS Pupil reflexes Focal motor deficit Seizure activity Toxin exposure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check a blood gas; look for hypoglycaemia (with a bedside ketone), sodium disturbance and hypocalcaemia.**
claims.source_text: Blood gas (capillary, venous, arterial) Hypoglycaemia (also perform bedside ketone for hyperketonaemia) Hypo, hypernatraemia Hypocalcaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider brain injury, stroke, meningitis/encephalitis and shunt complication; manage seizures.**
claims.source_text: Consider Brain injury Stroke Meningitis/Encephalitis Shunt complication Manage seizures
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine fully: temperature, rash, petechiae, purpura. Correct hypothermia**; manage pain.
claims.source_text: Assess child fully Temperature Hypo/hyperthermia Rash, petechiae, purpura Correct hypothermia Pain management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also consider** cardiac dysfunction or pericardial effusion (transthoracic echo), coagulopathy and **non-accidental injury**.
claims.source_text: Important considerations Cardiac dysfunction & pericardial effusion (consider transthoracic echocardiogram) Coagulopathy Non accidental injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get phone advice early from the specialised paediatric service**, review the history and examine thoroughly.
claims.source_text: Refer to and obtain phone advice early from local specialised paediatric service Review history and examine thoroughly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reassess regularly; maintain oxygenation and ventilation; aim for normal systolic BP, urine output, glucose, electrolytes and temperature**; monitor for end-organ damage; consider analgesia and sedation.
claims.source_text: Reassess regularly to monitor progress Maintain oxygenation and ventilation Aim normal systolic blood pressure, urine output, glucose, electrolytes, temperature Monitor for end organ damage Consider analgesia and sedation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Offer family members the option to be present**, ideally with a support person. **Offer debriefing to all staff involved.**
claims.source_text: Family members of patients undergoing resuscitation should be given the option to be present, ideally with an assigned support person. … Debriefing should be offered to all involved staff who wish to attend.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the local paediatric team for any child needing resuscitation**; consider transfer when care is beyond the hospital's comfort level.
claims.source_text: Consider Consultation with local paediatric team when: Any child requiring resuscitation Consider transfer when: Child requiring care beyond the comfort level of the hospital
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Resuscitation: Care of the seriously unwell child' (Last Updated May 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Resuscitation__Care_of_the_seriously_unwell_child/, retrieved 2026-09-23
